# Reproducible R Calculations {#sec-reproducible-r}

This appendix uses **base R**, allowing calculation checks without Shiny or additional packages. A runnable file is supplied in `scripts/reproduce-examples.R`, and an independently oriented smoke-check file in `scripts/check-examples.R`.

## Single proportion

```r
p <- 0.50
d <- 0.05
z <- qnorm(0.975)
n0 <- z^2 * p * (1 - p) / d^2
ceiling(n0) # 385 complete observations
```

## Finite population correction

```r
N <- 1000
n_fpc <- n0 / (1 + (n0 - 1) / N)
ceiling(n_fpc)
```

## Mean precision

```r
sd <- 10; precision <- 2
ceiling(qnorm(0.975)^2 * sd^2 / precision^2)
```

## Two mean groups: balanced approximate normal method

```r
sd <- 15; difference <- 5
alpha <- 0.05; power <- 0.80
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
z_power <- qnorm(power)
ceiling(2 * sd^2 * (z_alpha + z_power)^2 / difference^2)
```

## Sample-size sensitivity analysis

```r
precision_grid <- seq(0.03, 0.10, 0.005)
n_grid <- ceiling(qnorm(.975)^2 * .5 * .5 / precision_grid^2)
plot(precision_grid, n_grid, type = "b", xlab = "Absolute precision",
     ylab = "Complete sample size")
```

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
These are deliberately explicit approximations. A directly coded illustrative formula may not numerically match a software method using different null/alternative variances, interval construction or rounding. The book must record the precise method used for each final worked example.
:::
